clue.text: Crucial — and Kitty has the last word, with story unfinished

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, a fund
amen is the word that closes a prayer

indicators.note: unfinished says the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: Something vital is happening, and the cat gets the final say while the tale is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' suggests a cat but is a pool of money. 'unfinished' trims TALE to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something basic and essential, synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Shows off apartments housing a Parisian

indicators.note: housing means the word for apartments holds the French article inside it

parts.note: apartments are flats in British English
a Parisian would say un for 'a', the French indefinite article

explanation.surface: A property agent displays apartments that have a French resident living in them.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to display ostentatiously, a synonym for showing off.

clue.text: Detected rising attitudes one shows

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the hidden letters are read upwards, backwards
shows means the letters are on display within the words attitudes one

explanation.surface: Someone noticed attitudes improving, as one person demonstrates.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters DESON span 'attitudES ONe'; 'rising' turns them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose something out is to sniff it out, so nosed means sensed or found.

clue.text: Tacky substances he's found in adult nightclubs

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: found in means the letters of he's sit inside the word for nightclubs

parts.note: dives are seedy nightclubs or bars

explanation.surface: A seedy picture: tacky stuff a man discovers in sleazy adult clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacky' suggests cheap and vulgar but here means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Glues and gums are sticky, or tacky, materials.

clue.text: Warms up, removing top for food

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: to warm something up is to heat it

explanation.surface: Someone reheats leftovers, stripping off the top layer before serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is an informal noun for food, as in 'grab some eats'.

clue.text: Idle as credit gone

parts.note: on tick is British slang for on credit
over means finished or gone, as in 'the party is over'

explanation.surface: Someone is out of work now that their credit has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs slowly without doing work, idling.

clue.text: Tempted, but left university looking embarrassed

parts.note: an embarrassed face turns red

explanation.surface: A student was tempted away from studies, left college, and now blushes about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone is to entice them, so lured means enticed.

clue.text: Dictionary (American) incorporating one page for this complex character

indicators.note: incorporating means the dictionary-plus-American letters hold the next pieces inside them

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An American dictionary entry includes a page devoted to a famously complicated figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' points to the Freudian complex named after this Greek king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theban king who killed his father and wed his mother gives his name to Freud's complex.

clue.text: Go off with dog and escape

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: Someone sets off with their dog and runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb here, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom for running away from danger, fleeing.

clue.text: Tasteful number without a name?

indicators.note: without means those two letters are taken out of the word for number

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs, an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A wry question: is an anonymous figure in good taste?
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthetic choice concerns beauty and good taste, so the adjective fits tasteful.

clue.text: Some drinks and a single shot

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for a group
one bullet or one discharge of a gun

explanation.surface: A bar scene: a few drinks and one measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the drinks bought for everyone at once and one piece of ammunition.

clue.text: Brown backed first person in such a colony

indicators.note: backed means the colour word is turned round

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
first is written 1st, with I standing for the 1

explanation.surface: A man named Brown was the first to support some community or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such a colony' points to a naturist camp, home of the person defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist colony is home to those who live without clothes.

clue.text: Weather when fish will take line and bite?

indicators.note: will take means the fish word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: cod is a fish
to snap is to bite

explanation.surface: An angler asks what conditions make fish go for the line and bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden short spell of freezing conditions is a kind of weather.

clue.text: Tried very hard to wander, by the way

indicators.note: by means the wandering word sits beside the street abbreviation

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: Someone made a big effort to stroll along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make a great effort, and strove is its past tense.

clue.text: Weather that sees artist in decline

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a fall is a decline

explanation.surface: Bad conditions are blamed for a painter's career going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation such as a downpour is weather.

clue.text: Neat sign designed for perennials

indicators.note: designed means the letters of neat sign are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A tidy garden sign has been made for some long-lived plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are blue-flowered plants that live for several years, perennials.

clue.text: The sort of grouping that's not expensive, with duty to replace European Commission

indicators.note: to replace means the duty word goes where the Commission letters were

parts.note: economic can mean cheap or good value
a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: A politician talks about low-cost classification and a levy in place of Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxonomy is the science of classifying organisms into ranked groups.

clue.text: Bad, if one turns out to be genuine

indicators.note: turns out means the letters of bad if one are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something bad may yet prove to be authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'in good faith'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in good faith, from the Latin, is authentic and real.

clue.text: Careless mistake with wearing shoes

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake
shod means wearing shoes

explanation.surface: An error made while someone has their shoes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is done sloppily and without due care.

clue.text: Insult a naturopath, pinching eastern leader's wife

indicators.note: pinching means the words insult a naturopath hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: An alternative healer is insulted while the ruler's wife steals something.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is a Muslim ruler and his wife holds the matching title.

clue.text: Praises army officers after cut back

indicators.note: after means the officers come after the reversed word
back means the cutting word is read in reverse

parts.note: to axe is to cut
Lts are lieutenants

explanation.surface: Someone praises military officers once spending has been reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to glorify or extol them.

clue.text: Greek island area with small pastries

parts.note: Samos is an island in the Aegean

explanation.surface: A holiday snack: little pastries from a stretch of a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Samosas are fried triangular savoury pastries from South Asia.

clue.text: Fail to be moved, finding means of salvation

indicators.note: moved means the letters of fail to be are shifted around

explanation.surface: Failing to be emotionally touched, someone finds a way to be saved.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue vessel at sea is literally how people are saved from drowning.

clue.text: Fundamental degree (intentionally so)

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
sic, Latin for 'thus', marks a quoted error as deliberate

explanation.surface: A first degree is basic, and the clue says so on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Editors print 'sic' to show that an odd spelling is quoted as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and fundamental both mean forming the essential foundation.

clue.text: Suffering at home, with company

parts.note: in means at home
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: Unwell and stuck indoors, with visitors to keep someone company.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm describes someone weak or ailing, as through illness or age.

clue.text: Opening bars — popular with half of troops

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: half of means only the first three letters of troops are used

explanation.surface: A band's first notes are a hit with half the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music.

clue.text: Infection prominent during past years

indicators.note: during means the answer occurs within the words past years

explanation.surface: A disease was widespread in years gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an infected swelling on the eyelid, a visible inflammation.

clue.text: Finally docked to get a book of charts

indicators.note: docked means the phrase loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A ship has come in at last, and its crew collect their navigation book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship arriving but means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps.

clue.text: Suggests prisoners should swallow note

indicators.note: should swallow means the prisoners word takes the note inside it

parts.note: inmates are prisoners
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone proposes that jailed people eat a written message to hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to hint or imply indirectly.

clue.text: Bar in Cricket Club records intellectual

indicators.note: in means the bar word sits between the two letters of the club abbreviation

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise
logs are records

explanation.surface: A cricket club's bar keeps records of a brainy member.
explanation.walkthrough: Clever clogs is a mocking British name for a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever clogs is someone smart, often derisively, so a brainy person.
